embeds.title: 🟡 Mini Shai-Hulud Malware Campaign Resurfaces Across Hundreds of npm Packages
embeds.description:
**Actor:** TeamPCP
A self-replicating malware campaign known as Mini Shai-Hulud, attributed to TeamPCP, has resurfaced by embedding itself across hundreds of npm packages. The malware executes upon installation, harvests credentials (GitHub tokens, npm tokens, SSH keys, cloud provider credentials, database connection strings), installs persistent OS-level backdoors, and propagates autonomously to other packages accessible via stolen tokens. Researchers from Aikido Security and Socket report that affected packages include popular libraries such as AntV, TallyUI, echarts-for-react, and timeago.js. The campaign also targeted TanStack, UiPath, and MistralAI last week. Standard package removal does not eliminate attacker access due to embedded backdoors in developer tool settings and OS-level services.
